description:
> *This was generated by AI during a review of mayel/conjure (an LLM writes code, compile errors go back to it for a retry).*

A defk compile error reaches the caller as a plain `CompileError` (`file`, `line`, `description`). Its registry code (`clause-pattern`, `enum-reduce`, ...) appears only inside the message text, in the footer link `<page>#<code>`.

Tools and agents that compile kernels (an editor integration, an agent repair loop, `Code.compile_string/2` at run time, now documented in the deploying guide) have to parse the message to learn which error it was, then look up the why and fix in `docs/compile-errors.md`.

Idea: expose the code as data, so a caller can match on it and fetch the registry entry (`Defk.Errors`: code, why, fix) without parsing text. Open questions:
- a `Defk.CompileError` exception (with `code`, and maybe `kernel`) vs. keeping `CompileError` and adding a lookup from the message
- whether the code (and a lookup by code) becomes public API (ADR-0006)
- what the Elixir-mode / `Defk.Test` side should expose, if anything

Out of scope: an LLM generator or repair loop in defk itself.
title: Compile errors carry their code as data
